description: Canonical learning reasoning behavior for A.R.I.A. The Learning Engine determines what validated experience may contribute to future reasoning, how strongly that experience should influence learned patterns, and what distinctions must be preserved between observed history, empirical association, route performance, contextual experience, causal learning, and candidate canonical knowledge. It does not redefine Evidence, Confidence, Context, Hypothesis, Probability, Uncertainty, Validation, Decision, Routing, Memory, Relationships, or Case State contracts.

core_principle.statement: A.R.I.A. shall learn from demonstrated experience without converting repetition into truth. What happened, what appeared associated, what improved routing, what was causally demonstrated, and what is sufficiently authoritative to become canonical knowledge are separate questions and shall remain separate.
rules: A completed case is not automatically a trustworthy learning example.
A resolved case is not automatically a causally understood case.
Operational recovery is not automatically causal learning.
Action effectiveness is not automatically root-cause validation.
Repeated correlation is not automatically causation.
Repeated experience is not automatically canonical truth.
Learning strength shall reflect what was actually demonstrated.
Learning shall preserve applicable Context.
Learning shall preserve provenance and attribution when available.
Dependent or duplicated experience shall not create artificial frequency.
Contradictory experience shall remain visible.
Historical case facts shall not be rewritten when learned aggregates change.
Learned statistical patterns shall remain distinguishable from canonical technical knowledge.
Learning Engine shall report downstream implications through Orchestration rather than directly manipulating other reasoning engines.
The Learning Engine shall remain technically domain-independent.

persistence_boundary.principle: Learning Engine defines canonical learning behavior but shall not create a competing universal persistence contract unless an authoritative schema explicitly establishes one.
rules: Learning Engine shall not define a canonical learning_event object without an authoritative schema.
Learning Engine shall not define a canonical experience_ledger record without an authoritative schema.
Learning Engine shall not invent canonical IDs for learned entities unless an applicable schema establishes them.
Temporary learning assessments and candidate patterns may exist as reasoning outputs.
Persistent learned structures shall use schema-authorized contracts when available.
If a future Learning schema is established, this engine shall defer field names, IDs, statuses, and persistence semantics to that schema.
Historical source Evidence and case records shall remain independently identifiable from derived learned patterns.

learning_classes.description: Learning from what occurred in a specific case without asserting broader generalization.
Learning empirical occurrence frequency within applicable Context.
Learning recurring associations among symptoms, evidence, conditions, actions, outcomes, or other contextual factors.
Learning how diagnostic routes and route steps perform under applicable Context.
Learning the information value, effectiveness, cost, risk, or practical performance of Actions.
Learning how ordered diagnostic or corrective sequences perform.
Learning from sufficiently causally discriminating validated experience.
Learning from reappearance of a condition after prior correction or resolution.
Learning contextual patterns associated with users, teams, roles, or other participants without creating universal credibility judgments.
Learning contextual patterns associated with products, variants, manufacturers, configurations, environments, architectures, or other technical Context.
A proposed generalizable claim derived from accumulated experience that requires the applicable knowledge-governance process before becoming canonical.

learning_pipeline.name: IDENTIFY_LEARNING_SOURCE
learning_pipeline.description: Identify the case, event, Action, route, validation result, recurrence, or other experience from which learning is being considered.

learning_pipeline.name: RESOLVE_SOURCE_CONTEXT
learning_pipeline.description: Consume applicable canonical Context necessary to interpret and generalize the experience.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_SOURCE_EVIDENCE
learning_pipeline.description: Consume canonical Evidence assessments relevant to the experience.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_VALIDATION_STATE
learning_pipeline.description: Consume Validation results to determine what the experience actually demonstrated.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_CAUSAL_STATE
learning_pipeline.description: Determine whether causal attribution is demonstrated, merely supported, unresolved, or not applicable.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_RESOLUTION_STATE
learning_pipeline.description: Determine whether operational recovery, corrective effectiveness, stability, and durable resolution were sufficiently demonstrated.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_ATTRIBUTION
learning_pipeline.description: Determine whether actions, observations, decisions, or outcomes can be defensibly attributed to specific participants or entities.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_INDEPENDENCE_AND_DUPLICATION
learning_pipeline.description: Determine whether the experience represents an independent learning observation or duplicates/dependently reflects another underlying event.

learning_pipeline.name: CLASSIFY_ALLOWED_LEARNING
learning_pipeline.description: Determine which learning classes the experience can legitimately support.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_GENERALIZATION_SCOPE
learning_pipeline.description: Determine how broadly the experience may be generalized across Context.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_LEARNING_CONFIDENCE
learning_pipeline.description: Assess confidence in the proposed learning using the canonical confidence architecture.

learning_pipeline.name: ASSESS_LEARNING_INFLUENCE
learning_pipeline.description: Determine the relative influence the experience should have on learned patterns without defining competing probability mechanics.

learning_pipeline.name: CHECK_CONTRADICTIONS_AND_POISONING_RISK
learning_pipeline.description: Check for contradictory experience, duplication, manipulation, attribution problems, invalidated Evidence, or other contamination risks.

learning_pipeline.name: GENERATE_LEARNING_RESULT
learning_pipeline.description: Produce a scoped learning result that states what may be learned, what may not be learned, and why.

learning_pipeline.name: RETURN_LEARNING_RESULT
learning_pipeline.description: Return learned-pattern and downstream implications to Orchestration and applicable persistence/governance mechanisms.

learning_eligibility.principle: Learning eligibility is multidimensional. An experience may be suitable for one type of learning while being unsuitable for another.
rules: Eligibility concepts are reasoning classifications unless an authoritative schema establishes persisted statuses.
An experience may be ELIGIBLE for route learning while INSUFFICIENT for causal learning.
An experience may be ELIGIBLE for symptom-pattern learning while RESTRICTED for failure-frequency learning.
An unresolved root cause does not automatically exclude route-performance learning.
An ineffective Action may still be highly valuable for Action or route learning.
Invalidated source Evidence may exclude learning that depended on that Evidence.
Insufficient Context may restrict generalization without eliminating case-specific experience.
Learning Engine shall not collapse all learning eligibility into a single pass/fail gate.

validation_boundary.principle: Validation determines what the experience demonstrated. Learning determines what may defensibly be generalized from that demonstrated experience.
rules: Learning Engine shall consume Validation results rather than recreate validation logic.
Action completion alone supports only limited learning.
Action effectiveness may support Action-performance learning without supporting causal learning.
Symptom resolution may support operational-outcome learning without proving root cause.
Causal validation may support causal learning.
Stability validation may strengthen resolution and recurrence-related learning.
Regression-free validation may strengthen corrective-action learning.
Partial validation shall restrict learning to the demonstrated portion.
Inconclusive validation shall not be converted into validated causal learning.
Validation Confidence, Causal Confidence, and Resolution Confidence shall remain distinct inputs.

confidence_boundary.principle: Learning confidence shall use the canonical confidence architecture and shall not define a competing numeric confidence system.
rules: Learning Engine shall not define confidence ranges.
Learning Engine shall not define competing confidence labels.
Learning Confidence represents confidence that a proposed learned pattern is supported within its stated scope.
Learning Confidence shall remain scoped to the specific learning claim.
High Resolution Confidence does not imply high Causal Confidence.
High Causal Confidence does not imply broad generalizability.
Weak Context Confidence may constrain generalization.
Weak attribution confidence may constrain participant-specific learning.
Dependent observations shall constrain confidence in apparent repetition.
UNKNOWN shall remain UNKNOWN when confidence cannot meaningfully be established.

learning_influence.principle: Learned experience may have different influence based on demonstrated quality and applicability, but Learning Engine shall not create a competing universal numerical probability formula.
rules: Learning influence shall not be equivalent to raw case count.
A duplicated incident shall not receive independent influence merely because it appears in multiple records.
A highly applicable validated case may influence a learned pattern more than a weakly applicable case.
Recency may matter when the underlying system, process, population, or technical state changes over time.
Older experience shall not be discarded solely because it is old.
Learning Engine may provide qualitative or schema-authorized influence information.
Probability Engine owns numerical hypothesis probability updates.
Calibration mechanics remain outside Learning authority unless explicitly established by an authoritative contract.

case_experience_learning.principle: A case may contribute useful historical experience even when it cannot support broad statistical or causal generalization.
rules: Case history shall remain distinguishable from derived learned aggregates.
The historical case shall not be rewritten when future interpretation changes.
Later invalidation may change whether the case contributes to current learned patterns without erasing historical facts.
Case-specific learning may remain useful even when generalization is restricted.

frequency_learning.principle: A.R.I.A. may learn empirical occurrence frequency within sufficiently comparable Context, but empirical frequency is not universal technical truth.
rules: Frequency learning shall preserve applicable Context.
Frequency learning shall distinguish raw observation count from effective independent support.
Duplicate and dependent cases shall not inflate effective frequency.
Uncertain causal attribution shall constrain root-cause frequency learning.
A case may contribute to symptom frequency without qualifying for confirmed-cause frequency.
Changing populations, products, configurations, environments, processes, or other material Context may reduce historical applicability.
Frequency learning shall remain empirical experience.
Probability Engine determines how learned frequency influences current hypothesis probability.
Pattern learning shall preserve sample size and effective independent support when available.
Pattern learning shall preserve applicable Context.
Association shall not automatically be labeled causal.
Rare patterns shall not be overstated.
Contradictory examples shall remain represented.
A strong empirical pattern may generate a candidate knowledge claim.
Pattern learning shall not directly create canonical Relationships.

route_learning.principle: A.R.I.A. may learn how diagnostic routes and route steps perform, including whether they produced useful information even when they did not directly resolve the case.
rules: Route success and diagnosis correctness are separate learning dimensions.
An Action that eliminates a hypothesis may be diagnostically successful.
An Action that produces no useful information may be a poor route step even when easy to perform.
A slower Action may remain preferable when it provides materially greater discrimination or lower risk.
Route performance shall preserve Context.
Failed routes remain valuable learning data.
Learning Engine shall not directly alter current route costs.
Routing Engine determines current route behavior using applicable learned information.

action_learning.principle: A.R.I.A. may learn the historical technical and operational performance of Actions without confusing Action completion, information value, effectiveness, and causal proof.
rules: Action completion does not establish effectiveness.
Action effectiveness does not establish causality.
An ineffective Action may still have high diagnostic value.
An Action may have different historical performance in different Context.
Action learning shall not directly select the next Action.
Decision Engine owns current Action selection.

sequence_learning.principle: A.R.I.A. may learn how ordered sequences of diagnostic or corrective Actions perform without converting learned sequences into mandatory static troubleshooting trees.
rules: Sequence performance shall preserve applicable Context.
Shorter sequences are not automatically better.
Faster sequences are not automatically better.
A sequence with greater safety or diagnostic reliability may be preferred despite greater duration.
Sequence learning shall remain advisory learned experience.
Routing Engine owns route construction and route selection.

causal_learning.principle: Causal learning requires evidence that meaningfully discriminates causal mechanisms, not merely temporal association or successful recovery.
rules: Causal learning shall consume causal validation rather than recreate it.
Operational recovery alone shall not support strong causal learning.
Multiple simultaneous interventions shall constrain attribution to any individual change.
Repeated controlled causal observations may strengthen empirical causal learning.
A causal pattern learned from one Context shall not automatically generalize to materially different Context.
Causal learning may support a candidate canonical claim.
Causal learning shall not directly create a canonical causal Relationship.

recurrence_learning.principle: Recurrence provides evidence about durability, completeness of correction, hidden contributing mechanisms, and future risk.
rules: Recurrence after apparent resolution shall remain linked to the prior resolution history when the relationship is supported.
Recurrence may reduce confidence in the completeness or durability of the previous correction.
Recurrence does not automatically prove that the prior diagnosis was wrong.
Recurrence may indicate incomplete correction, multiple causes, environmental dependence, degradation, reintroduction, or a new failure.
Time to recurrence shall be preserved when available.
Repeated recurrence patterns may become important learned experience.
Recurrence shall not automatically be counted as an independent failure when it is merely continued manifestation of the same unresolved event.

participant_learning.principle: A.R.I.A. may learn contextual patterns associated with participants only when attribution is sufficiently supported and only within the demonstrated scope.
rules: Participant learning shall remain contextual.
A.R.I.A. shall not create one universal competence score.
A.R.I.A. shall not create one universal credibility score.
Reporter identity shall not imply fault.
Case ownership shall not imply technical responsibility.
When attribution is unknown, A.R.I.A. shall not invent individual responsibility.
Shared work may attribute different observations and Actions to different participants.
Attribution Confidence shall constrain participant-specific learning.
Improvement over time shall be representable.
Recent validated performance may reduce applicability of older participant patterns.
Participant-specific learned experience shall not override stronger direct Evidence.
Personal judgment labels shall not be stored as technical learning.

technical_context_learning.principle: A.R.I.A. may learn patterns associated with technical Context while avoiding unsupported generalization.
rules: The applicable canonical Context architecture determines actual context representation.
This list does not create a competing Context vocabulary.
Patterns associated with a manufacturer or product shall remain empirical unless canonically validated.
A product-specific pattern shall not automatically generalize to a manufacturer.
A manufacturer-specific pattern shall not automatically generalize to a domain.
Revision-specific behavior shall remain revision-specific when material.
Context generalization shall expand only when supporting experience justifies broader scope.

generalization.principle: Learning shall generalize no more broadly than the supporting experience justifies.
rules: Scope levels are reasoning concepts unless established by an authoritative schema.
Broader scope requires evidence spanning the dimensions being generalized across.
Repeated observations from one product variant do not automatically establish a product-family rule.
Repeated observations from one organization do not automatically establish a universal rule.
Context diversity may strengthen justified generalization.
Material contradictions across Context shall constrain generalization.
A.R.I.A. shall prefer narrower defensible learning over broader unsupported learning.
Duplicate detection may flag experience for review or reduced independent influence.
Multiple records describing the same underlying event shall not be treated as independent observations.
Multiple cases derived from the same source Evidence shall preserve dependency.
Repeated human reports of one underlying condition shall not automatically create multiple independent failures.
Genuinely separate recurrences may remain distinct observations.
Evidence Engine remains authoritative for Evidence independence semantics.
Learning Engine evaluates independence at the experience/generalization level.

anti_poisoning.principle: A.R.I.A. shall resist learned-belief corruption caused by weak, duplicated, manipulated, misattributed, invalidated, or systematically biased experience.
rules: Repeated copies of the same claim shall not manufacture historical support.
Cases with unresolved cause shall not receive unrestricted causal-learning influence.
Learning dependent on invalidated Evidence shall be reassessed.
Misattributed participant behavior shall not become participant learning.
Sudden extreme learned-pattern changes should remain detectable.
Systematic data-source bias shall be considered when detectable.
High volume from one source shall not automatically outweigh stronger independent contradictory experience.
Learning shall remain reversible at the derived-pattern level when its support is later invalidated.

contradiction_handling.principle: Learned experience may legitimately disagree. Contradiction shall be analyzed rather than erased.
rules: Contradictory cases shall remain represented.
Contradiction may indicate Context differences.
Contradiction may indicate multiple causal mechanisms.
Contradiction may indicate measurement or attribution problems.
Contradiction may indicate temporal change in the underlying population or system.
A newer case shall not automatically overwrite older experience.
A more authoritative canonical source shall not erase empirical field experience; the disagreement shall remain distinguishable.
Material contradiction shall constrain Learning Confidence or generalization when appropriate.

probability_boundary.principle: Learning provides empirical historical information and learned patterns; Probability Engine determines how those inputs affect current belief.
rules: Learning Engine shall not directly assign current hypothesis probability.
Learning Engine shall not directly normalize competing hypotheses.
Learning Engine shall not define universal prior formulas.
Learned frequency may be an input to Probability reasoning.
Learned contextual patterns may be an input to Probability reasoning.
Probability Engine determines applicability, regularization, calibration, and numerical belief updates.
Historical frequency shall not override direct current-case Evidence.
Learning results shall be returned through Orchestration.

evidence_boundary.principle: Learning consumes Evidence and may produce derived experience patterns, but Evidence Engine owns Evidence semantics.
rules: Learning Engine shall not redefine canonical Evidence.
Learning Engine shall not redefine evidence quality.
Learning Engine shall not redefine evidence verification.
Learning Engine shall not redefine evidence independence.
Learning Engine shall not redefine evidence contradiction or invalidation.
Learning shall consume Evidence provenance where applicable.
A learned pattern is not automatically Evidence of a current-case fact.
A learned pattern may inform reasoning about what Evidence to seek.
Current direct Evidence may outweigh learned historical patterns.

context_boundary.principle: Learning preserves and reasons over Context but does not create a competing Context system.
rules: Context Engine owns canonical Context resolution.
Learning Engine shall not define competing context types.
Learning Engine shall not define competing context schemas.
Learning Engine may assess similarity between source Context and target Context.
Context mismatch shall constrain generalization.
Unknown material Context shall preserve generalization uncertainty.

hypothesis_boundary.principle: Learned experience may influence future hypothesis generation and ranking through the appropriate reasoning engines but shall not directly manipulate hypothesis state.
rules: Learning Engine shall not create canonical hyp_<UUID> records.
Learning Engine shall not confirm current hypotheses.
Learning Engine shall not eliminate current hypotheses.
Learned patterns may inform Hypothesis Engine.
Historical failure frequency may inform hypothesis generation.
Historical symptom patterns may inform hypothesis generation.
Hypothesis Engine owns hypothesis creation and state transitions.

uncertainty_boundary.principle: Learned experience may reduce or expose uncertainty, but Uncertainty Engine owns uncertainty reasoning.
rules: Learning Engine shall not define a competing uncertainty persistence model.
Strong historical patterns may reduce uncertainty about where to investigate.
Conflicting learned patterns may increase Model Uncertainty.
Sparse experience may preserve uncertainty.
Context mismatch may preserve applicability uncertainty.
Learning Engine shall return uncertainty-relevant implications through Orchestration.

decision_boundary.principle: Learned Action performance may inform decisions, but Decision Engine owns Action selection.
rules: Learning Engine shall not select act_<UUID>.
Learning Engine may provide historical Action effectiveness or information-value patterns.
Learning Engine may provide historical risk, effort, or outcome patterns.
Decision Engine determines whether those learned patterns are applicable to the current case.
Current safety and case-specific constraints shall not be overridden by historical popularity.

routing_boundary.principle: Learned route performance informs Routing; Routing Engine owns current route construction, costing, and progression.
rules: Learning Engine shall not directly create route steps.
Learning Engine shall not directly change route costs.
Learning Engine shall not directly select next hops.
Learning Engine shall not directly reroute.
Learning Engine may report historical route-performance patterns.
Routing Engine determines current applicability and route behavior.

case_state_boundary.principle: Learning consumes case outcomes and demonstrated state but does not own lifecycle state.
rules: Learning Engine shall not mark a case resolved.
Learning Engine shall not close a case.
Learning Engine shall not reopen a case.
Learning Engine shall not change case reasoning state.
Case State supplies applicable case outcome and lifecycle information.
Learning eligibility shall not substitute for case lifecycle state.

memory_boundary.principle: Learning determines what experience means and what may be generalized. Memory determines how authorized information is retained and retrieved.
rules: Learning Engine shall not independently define memory tiers.
Learning Engine shall not independently define memory retention periods.
Learning Engine shall not independently promote information into persistent Memory.
Learning Engine may identify learning results that are candidates for retention.
Memory Engine determines persistence and retrieval behavior under its authoritative contract.
A learned pattern and a remembered case are not the same thing.

canonical_knowledge_boundary.principle: Experience-derived learning may propose canonical knowledge but shall not silently promote itself into canonical truth.
rules: Learning Engine may generate candidate knowledge claims.
Candidate knowledge shall remain distinguishable from canonical knowledge.
Repeated association shall not automatically create a causal Relationship.
Repeated causal validation may strengthen a candidate causal claim.
Canonical Relationships shall not be created or mutated directly by Learning Engine.
Canonical knowledge promotion requires the applicable governance authority.
Conflicts with existing canonical knowledge shall trigger review rather than silent overwrite.
Supporting and contradicting experience shall remain auditable.

orchestration_boundary.principle: Learning Engine produces learning results. Orchestration coordinates their effects on other reasoning components.
rules: Learning Engine shall not directly invoke every affected engine.
New learned patterns shall be returned through Orchestration.
Material changes to learned frequency shall be returned through Orchestration.
Material route-performance learning shall be returned through Orchestration.
Material Action-performance learning shall be returned through Orchestration.
Candidate knowledge claims shall be returned through the applicable governance path.
Orchestration determines whether Probability, Hypothesis, Decision, Routing, Memory, or other components require reevaluation.

reassessment_rules: Derived learning shall be reassessed when material support changes.
Historical source records shall remain immutable except through their own authoritative correction mechanisms.
Invalidated support shall no longer contribute as valid current support.
New contradictions may reduce confidence or narrow generalization.
New diverse support may justify broader generalization.
Duplicate discovery may reduce effective support without deleting historical records.
Changes to derived learning shall remain explainable.

rules: Outputs are reasoning results unless an authoritative schema establishes corresponding persisted fields.
Learning outputs shall state their applicable scope.
Learning outputs shall distinguish association from causation.
Learning outputs shall distinguish case history from learned aggregate.
Learning outputs shall distinguish empirical learning from canonical knowledge.
Learning outputs shall preserve material restrictions.
Learning outputs shall preserve material contradictions.
Learning outputs shall not invent Evidence IDs or case IDs.
Learning outputs shall not calculate current hypothesis probability.
Learning outputs shall not select Actions.
Learning outputs shall not perform Routing.
Learning outputs shall not change case lifecycle state.
Learning outputs shall not directly promote canonical knowledge.

required_questions: What experience is A.R.I.A. learning from?
What was actually demonstrated in that experience?
What type of learning is supported?
What type of learning is not supported?
Is the experience independent or duplicated?
How strong is the supporting Evidence?
Was causality demonstrated or merely associated?
Was the resolution stable and durable?
How broadly can the result be generalized?
How confident is A.R.I.A. in the learned pattern?
Is this empirical experience or candidate canonical knowledge?
rules: Learning explanations shall not overstate causal meaning.
Learning explanations shall identify important scope restrictions.
Learning explanations shall identify material contradictions.
Learning explanations shall identify when duplicate or dependent experience reduces effective support.
Learning explanations shall distinguish validated facts from statistical patterns and candidate knowledge.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine creates a competing universal persistence contract.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep persistence schema-authorized and separate from reasoning behavior.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine creates its own confidence range or labels.
failure_modes.prevention: Consume Core/Registries/confidence_levels.json.

failure_modes.description: A resolved case is treated as a causally validated case.
failure_modes.prevention: Consume Validation's separate operational, causal, stability, and resolution assessments.

failure_modes.description: A successful Action is treated as proof of the suspected root cause.
failure_modes.prevention: Require causal discrimination for causal learning.

failure_modes.description: Repeated association is promoted into causal truth.
failure_modes.prevention: Preserve association and causation as separate learning classes.

failure_modes.description: Historical occurrence frequency is treated as universal technical truth.
failure_modes.prevention: Preserve empirical frequency as contextual experience.

failure_modes.description: Raw record count is treated as independent statistical support.
failure_modes.prevention: Assess duplication, dependence, and effective support.

failure_modes.description: Multiple records of the same incident inflate learned frequency.
failure_modes.prevention: Detect and preserve duplicate/dependent relationships.

failure_modes.description: Experience from materially different Context is aggregated as though directly comparable.
failure_modes.prevention: Preserve Context and restrict generalization.

failure_modes.description: Narrow experience is generalized beyond supported scope.
failure_modes.prevention: Require support across dimensions being generalized.

failure_modes.description: Contextual participant learning becomes a universal human credibility or competence judgment.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep participant learning contextual, attributable, and multidimensional.

failure_modes.description: The person reporting a problem is treated as responsible for causing it.
failure_modes.prevention: Preserve action and observation attribution separately.

failure_modes.description: Past case facts are rewritten when current learned interpretation changes.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep source history immutable and derived learning recalculable.

failure_modes.description: Contradictory experience is discarded to preserve a preferred learned pattern.
failure_modes.prevention: Preserve contradiction and adjust confidence or scope.

failure_modes.description: Learning continues to rely on Evidence that has been invalidated or retracted.
failure_modes.prevention: Trigger reassessment when source support changes.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine directly calculates current hypothesis probabilities or universal priors.
failure_modes.prevention: Return learned empirical inputs to Probability through Orchestration.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine directly creates, confirms, or eliminates current-case hypotheses.
failure_modes.prevention: Hypothesis Engine owns hypothesis state.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine directly selects the current Action.
failure_modes.prevention: Decision Engine owns Action selection.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine directly changes current route costs, next hops, or progression.
failure_modes.prevention: Routing Engine owns current routing behavior.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine recreates validation logic to decide what was demonstrated.
failure_modes.prevention: Consume Validation Engine outputs.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine recreates Evidence quality, verification, independence, or contradiction semantics.
failure_modes.prevention: Consume Evidence Engine assessments.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine creates a competing Context vocabulary or schema.
failure_modes.prevention: Consume canonical Context.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine independently decides permanent retention or retrieval behavior.
failure_modes.prevention: Memory Engine owns memory behavior.

failure_modes.description: Learning Engine directly promotes empirical patterns into canonical knowledge or Relationships.
failure_modes.prevention: Generate candidate claims and use the applicable governance process.

failure_modes.description: Universal Learning Engine hardcodes a particular technology, vendor, product, customer, organization, or named user.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep universal learning behavior domain-independent.

Operational resolution remains distinct from causal validation.
Action effectiveness remains distinct from causal proof.
Association remains distinct from causation.
Empirical frequency remains distinct from canonical truth.
Learned patterns preserve applicable Context.
Duplicate or dependent experience does not create artificial independent support.
Historical source records remain distinguishable from derived learned patterns.
Material contradictory experience remains represented.
Learning generalizes no more broadly than supporting experience justifies.
Confidence vocabulary and ranges are owned by Core/Registries/confidence_levels.json.
Learning Engine does not create a competing universal learning persistence schema.
Learning Engine consumes rather than recreates Validation semantics.
Learning Engine consumes rather than recreates Evidence semantics.
Learning Engine consumes rather than recreates Context semantics.
Learning Engine does not calculate current hypothesis probability.
Learning Engine does not directly manipulate current hypothesis state.
Learning Engine does not select current Actions.
Learning Engine does not perform current Routing.
Learning Engine does not directly change case lifecycle or reasoning state.
Learning Engine does not independently define Memory persistence or retrieval policy.
Learning Engine does not directly promote empirical learning into canonical knowledge.
Participant learning remains contextual and does not become a universal credibility score.
Material learning results are returned through Orchestration for downstream coordination.
Learning Engine remains technically domain-independent.

Treating Action completion as Action effectiveness.

Treating symptom resolution as root-cause proof.
Treating correlation as causation.
Treating historical frequency as universal truth.
Treating raw record count as independent statistical support.
Counting duplicate cases as independent learning observations.
Counting dependent observations as independent support.
Ignoring material Context differences during aggregation.
Generalizing beyond supported Context.
Creating a universal participant competence score.
Creating a universal participant credibility score.
Assigning fault based solely on reporter identity.
Rewriting historical case facts because learned interpretation changed.
Erasing contradictory experience.
Continuing to rely on invalidated Evidence without reassessment.
Directly calculating current hypothesis probability.
Directly creating universal numerical prior formulas.
Directly creating, confirming, or eliminating current-case hypotheses.
Directly selecting act_<UUID>.
Directly creating route steps.
Directly changing route costs.
Directly selecting route next hops.
Directly rerouting.
Recreating Validation result semantics.
Recreating Evidence quality, verification, provenance, contradiction, or independence semantics.
Creating competing Context types or schemas.
